title: KINETIC
summary: Three kinds of work (a piston being fitted, a mallet and wedge, a tire-bead machine) share seven seconds of one sung work verse, then it breaks. A refinery worker, a man waiting beside hot rail in Belo Horizonte, a complete interval at a machine, and a hand that stops.

reviews.text:
VERDICT: reference stronger (leaning inconclusive on sound; I cannot hear the film, so the "original sound phrase" and any coordination by sound go unjudged).

Noticed before the brief: at 0:17-0:24 the film cuts between a log and a mallet (0:17-0:19, 0:23-0:24), the mallet worker (0:20) and the engine-block hand (0:21). Then at 0:22 it cuts back to the woman at the wheel, with the cuts landing on the narration "mallet... carpenter". It reads as one repeated beat, but the transcript's talk of tires, stools and "oil business" does not describe what the frames show (engine blocks, a furnace). That mismatch is probably recogniser error in the hiss, so I treat it as unreliable.

Largest gap: the brief wants an interruption kept at normal speed, and I see none. The sheet shows only continuous labor across 44s. The "interruption" at 0:17-0:19 is a static log with no worker. It is an insert, not a maintenance interval, and it lasts about 3 seconds. The target is 90s and this is 44s. The loudness data shows nothing that reads as a coordination phrase, and a drop to -45.9 dB at 42s suggests an abrupt end. The ending at 0:42-0:43 is the mallet worker again, still working. Nothing stops, so the brief's end condition is unmet.

Repairs:
1. 0:17-0:19: replace the log insert with one complete waiting or maintenance shot of 6s or more at real speed. Check that a worker is visibly idle or tending the machine.
2. 0:42-0:43: end on a stopped hand or machine. Check that the last frame shows no motion.
3. 0:25-0:35: add one wide contextual shot. Check that it shows what the close crop at 0:09-0:16 left out.

Protect: the 0:36-0:41 engine-block sequence with the 0:42 return to the mallet worker. It shows a changed framing on return.
reviews.builder_note: True: nothing in the first cut was an interval. A whole 10.8 s interval from Master Hands was added, and the film now ends on a stopped hand.

reviews.text:
VERDICT: reference stronger (a pass is not earned). I cannot hear the film; the sound phrase and any rhythm coordination are unjudged. Speech recognition in the hiss is partly unreliable.

Noticed before the brief: 17.1-18.3 is a hard cut to a static wood block on a stump. By 19.6 it returns to the mallet worker from 4.9-7.3, so the film recycles the same clips. The narration is also mismatched. "Carpenter... stool" (5.7-9.1) plays over a woman at a machine, and "tire... flipper" (9.1-17.2) plays over the same woman. The ASR lines are loose, but they do not match the pictures.

Largest gap: there are no three distinct processes with an established repeated movement. Cylinder-block hands, the mallet worker, the woman at the wheel, the hard-hat worker, the machine operator and the furnace all get one or two brief appearances. No beat is visibly repeated, and no maintenance or waiting interval appears (30.5-40.3 is a continuous task). There is no return that reveals excluded framing. The ending at 54.9-57.4 is a static hand close-up, not a worker or machine stopping.

Repairs:
1. Cut the sheet to three processes, with 3 or more visible repetitions each by 0-30s. Check: each process appears in at least 3 shots, with the same action visible in each.
2. Hold one maintenance or wait shot unbroken for 4s or more at normal speed, around 30.5-40.3. Check: one continuous shot with no cut and a visible pause in the work.
3. Replace 54.9-57.4 with a wider re-frame of the 4.9-7.3 mallet worker, ending on the mallet stopping. Check: the frame is wider than at 4.9 and shows the mallet at rest.

Strength to protect: the high-contrast black-and-white texture and the hands-and-machinery close-ups (0-3.7, 46.4-51.3) read clearly as labor.
reviews.builder_note: The critic wants three processes, each with at least three visible repetitions. The film shows each process in one or two short shots; that is below the brief and was not repaired.
